meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pancake, blin' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда положите мне ещё парочку блинов!
examples.trans: Then serve me a couple more pancakes!

examples.text: Большое спасибо вам за вкусные блины.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the delicious pancakes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'будить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wake (someone) up', paired with 'будить'.

related.gloss: not to to wake up (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: What if we wake him up?

examples.text: А вдруг мы его разбудим? И у него начнутся боли?
examples.trans: What if we wake him up? And what if his pains start?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'together', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'dessert' (from 'desservir', to clear the table).

examples.text: Гости в зале уже спрашивают новые десерты.
examples.trans: Guests in the dining room are already asking for new desserts.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pleasant, nice').

examples.trans: Very well! Have a pleasant evening.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'appetite' in everyday Russian.
High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some, some kind of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'юрприз'). Common masculine noun meaning 'surprise' in everyday Russian.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'видеть'.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pastry chef, confectioner' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Our pastry chef made a cake.
Here is dessert from our pastry chef.

examples.text: Я пришёл к нашему кондитеру Луи!
examples.trans: I arrived at our pastry chef Louis's place!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something, a thing or two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I want to show you something.

examples.text: И ещё кое-что. Эдуард Владимирович просил передать привет.
examples.trans: And one more thing. Eduard Vladimirovich asked us to pass on his regards.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'button' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Even a button on the shirt was torn off.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть пуговица.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always button.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?

просить.gloss: to ask, to request, to beg

meanings.en: to ask, to request, to beg
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask, to request, to beg', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Samsonov, I asked you not to!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'позже').

examples.trans: Let us talk a bit later.
Let us go to the cinema a bit later.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

потрудиться.gloss: to take the trouble, to bother

meanings.en: to take the trouble, to bother
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'трудиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take the trouble, to bother', paired with 'трудиться'.

examples.trans: Kindly do not bother me anymore!

examples.text: Я ничего не защемила! Потрудитесь меня больше не беспокоить!
examples.trans: I didn't pinch anything! Kindly don't bother me anymore!

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ъяснить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to explain', paired with 'объяснять'.

examples.trans: I will explain everything to you right now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!
